summary: Freeland Heights lookout, Luzerne County: register says a steel P tower was used 1925-1927 and replaced in 1928, while 1927 newspapers describe a new steel tower after lightning. Now a former site.

facts.design: Steel tower; the register calls it a steel P tower
facts.status_note: Listed as a former fire lookout site. No removal date found in the sources read.

staffing.status: crew stationed in 1930; operators named in 1939 and 1955

facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Forest and Waters

events.note: Register dates use of the steel P tower from 1925
Older wooden structure destroyed by a lightning strike some months before November 1927
Work on a new steel tower at Freeland Heights began in November 1927 (notice of November 23, 1927); one notice gives 80 ft, another 85 ft
Register says the P tower was replaced in 1928
April 1930: crew of fire fighters stationed at the lookout tower on Freeland Heights, to handle forest fires in that section
July 1939: Louis Corazza named as fire tower man at Freeland
April 1955: Frank Swankoski listed as operator
Registered September 16, 2008, nominated by Henry Isenberg
City-Data listing of FCC records: Freeland Fire Tower radio license granted to Pennsylvania's Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, September 20, 2011

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register: steel P tower used 1925-1927 and replaced in 1928. 1927 newspapers: an older wooden structure was destroyed by lightning and a new steel tower was begun in November 1927. The story reports both.
One 1927 notice gives 80 feet and another 85 feet. Facts use 80 feet (24.4 m), the figure in the brief; the story gives both.

sources.title: FCC Registered Land Mobile Towers in Freeland, Pennsylvania

notes_for_editor: Brief height 24.4 m matches the 80 ft figure; the 85 ft figure disagrees. The FCC entry comes from City-Data, a copy of FCC data; check FCC ULS call sign KDX454 before relying on it. No source describes the site now. Access left out: no source gives it.
